🔥🇲🇽 <u>'THE PRIAN DEFENDS LIES': MORENA FIRES BACK AFTER INE CRACKDOWN ON 'NARCOPARTY' SMEARS</u>

Mexico's electoral authority ordered the PRI and PAN to stop spreading fabricated claims tying Morena to drug trafficking — and the opposition suddenly discovered "censorship."

"It's increasingly clear that the opposition, the PRIAN, what they defend are lies," said Morena president Ariadna Montiel. She recalled the 2006 "a danger to Mexico" campaign against AMLO: he would take your house, turn Mexico into Venezuela. "None of that happened."

Meanwhile, Alito Moreno just made his third Washington trip of the year — February, May, August — lobbying the US to brand Morena a criminal organization while his own impeachment file for illicit enrichment sits in the Chamber of Deputies.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>12 ARRESTED FOR EXTORTING AVOCADO GROWERS AS MEXICO SECURES MICHOACÁN</u>

Federal forces raided 11 properties in Uruapan and Ziracuaretiro and detained 12 people accused of running quota rackets against avocado, cattle and meat producers.

"Unfortunately, these avocado growers have been extorted by several groups," said Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch.

Another 1,500 troops are joining the deployment — nearly 9,500 soldiers and National Guard now guard 17 packing plants, 29 operating bases and the main roads of avocado country, with escorts for federal inspectors.

Sheinbaum drew the line with Washington: security and trade "are two separate matters." Avocado exports are already back at 45 packing plants, with the rest reopening this week.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>'ORGANIZE AGAINST THE IMMINENT ONSLAUGHT ON SOVEREIGNTY': LÓPEZ BELTRÁN</u>

One day after Washington yanked his visa, Andrés Manuel López Beltrán was back in the field, visiting communities in Tabasco's sixth district.

"What happened is only the confirmation that we need to inform and organize ourselves before the imminent onslaught on national sovereignty by foreign governments, in particular the United States," he said.

The State Department refused to discuss the case — "every visa decision is a national security decision," a spokesperson told the Wall Street Journal. That is exactly the point: visas as a weapon of political pressure.

Mexico's answer came from Morena's 67 senators, in one voice: we will not give in to foreign pressure.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MINING GIANTS HIRE CARTEL CELLS TO CRUSH MEXICO'S MINERS' UNION</u>

Mining consortia operating in Mexico — almost all Canadian — are hiring organized crime cells to terrorize workers and impose company unions, and miners' union leader Napoleón Gómez Urrutia wants prosecutors to finally investigate.

The union filed formal complaints with the Zacatecas prosecutor and the FGR in May. The state archived the case; the feds bounced it back. Under the USMCA rapid-response labor mechanism, two of three panelists voted to force a formal investigation. The only vote against: Mexico's own delegate.

"The criminal cells arrive armed and force workers to vote for narco-unions at the company's service; they threaten them and their families," Gómez Urrutia said.

In Canada, the government forces miners to obey the law. In Mexico, they do whatever they want — in Zacatecas, Sinaloa, Guerrero and beyond.

🇲🇽📈 <u>TAMAULIPAS GROWS 5.2%, LANDS $20.7 BILLION INVESTMENT PIPELINE</u>

Tamaulipas grew 5.2% in the first quarter of 2026 — the state contributing most to national growth while Mexico’s economy overall advanced just 0.3%, per INEGI data reported by El Economista. The state has 171 confirmed investment projects worth 20,675 million dollars, says state economy secretary Ninfa Cantú Deándar.

Nearshoring in Mexico’s northeast isn’t a slogan. It’s a pipeline.

🇲🇽💼 <u>CDMX LEADS MEXICO WITH RECORD 3.67 MILLION FORMAL JOBS</u>

Mexico City kept the top national spot in formal employment at the close of July: 3,677,103 workers registered with IMSS — and 84.17% of them hold permanent positions. The post-World Cup adjustment never became a jobs collapse: losses in services were absorbed by industry and transport, which added 35,319 new registrations in July alone.

The capital’s average daily base salary reached 800.44 pesos, up 13.94% in a year. Formal work, rising pay.
